proposal.rationale: Proposal: test transfer of a rule-based engine that reads Gerber files and a netlist, extracts geometric emission-risk features (trace-to-plane spacing, clock routing, decoupling placement, via stubs) and outputs a score plus violation list. Hypothesis: these rules may flag Nexara's 150–450 MHz hotspots and give engineers a self-run pre-sign-off check. Transfer is unproven: the tool was validated on other boards against CISPR 22 Class B, shows a 22% false-positive rate, and is described as an early gate, so Nexara's five boards must test generalisation.

facts.quote: Three of our last five PCB designs failed radiated emissions at a third-party EMC lab on the first submission, typically between 150–450 MHz
one senior hardware engineer and one firmware engineer part-time to a collaborative project, with access to our lab equipment and internal board archives under NDA
We have the Gerber files, BOM, and pre-compliance scan data for all five boards and would be willing to share them under NDA.
Ideally we want a layout checklist or a simulation workflow that our engineers can run themselves before sign-off
We have HyperLynx licences but our layout engineers mainly use them for impedance checks rather than full emissions prediction.
rule-based layout scoring tool that ingests Gerber files and a netlist, extracts geometric features related to emission risk, and outputs a numerical score and flagged violation list
covering trace-to-plane spacing, clock trace routing distance from board edge, decoupling capacitor placement relative to device power pins, and via stub length
boards that failed CISPR 22 Class B measurements scored below the threshold in 19 out of 23 cases (83% sensitivity). False-positive rate was 22%.
The tool is intended as an early design gate rather than a replacement for simulation or pre-compliance measurement.
joint projects combining academic simulation with industrial prototype testing; industrial PhD supervision for engineers at electronics companies
Her scanning bench is available for external use on a cost-recovery basis when faculty teaching commitments permit.

plan.question: Joint-project topic: can layout-scoring rules locate the 150–450 MHz hotspots of Nexara's five archived boards before testing? Conditional post-pilot industrial PhD question, only if go: which calibrated rule set predicts emissions on new boards?
plan.experiment: Baseline: Nexara's existing scans and lab outcomes. Weeks 1–12: score all five boards blind to results using a threshold fixed in advance, compare flagged violations with scan hotspots. Add HyperLynx emission checks only if kickoff verification shows the licences support them; otherwise drop.
plan.metrics: Kickoff pre-check: scans must give peak frequencies or locations mappable to layout features; failure is no-go for hotspot comparison. Coincidence: flagged feature within 20 mm of a hotspot or at a harmonic inside a scan peak band. Go: threshold not tuned on these boards; at least 2 of 3 failed boards flagged; at most 1 of 2 passed boards flagged; at most 10 unmatched violations per board. Negotiable.
plan.companyAsk: If approved internally, Nexara would assign part-time hardware and firmware engineers, supply board data under NDA, name an access owner, verify HyperLynx capability, and join weekly reviews. Hardware lead owns scan interpretation; firmware engineer owns scripting. Nothing is secured yet.
plan.researcherAsk: If available, Prof. Radulović would fix the threshold, adapt the rules, run the scoring, document the rule logic and advise on analysis. Scanning bench use would be requested only if schedule and cost-recovery terms are agreed.
plan.dataRequired: Requested under NDA: Gerber files, BOM, stackups, pre-compliance scans (peaks, locations) and lab pass/fail reports for five boards. Netlists are not confirmed; fallback: regenerate from design files, else narrow scope to Gerber-only rules. Access owner: Nexara hardware lead. Gates: written NDA, data-minimisation review, storage confirmation.
plan.milestones: Month 1 (weeks 1–4): NDA, data inventory, scan pre-check, netlist and HyperLynx checks, threshold fixed; owner both leads. Month 2 (weeks 5–8): blind scores and hotspot report; owner researcher. Month 3 (weeks 9–12): optional HyperLynx test, checklist draft, go/no-go memo; owners both.
plan.risks: Unknown: data completeness, researcher availability, rule transfer. Five boards limit statistical power; 22% false positives may burden engineers; scans may not map to layout features; scanning bench depends on teaching commitments.
plan.meeting: First-week actions: Nexara names access owner, drafts NDA and checks scans, netlists and HyperLynx; researcher drafts blind protocol and threshold. Agenda: goals, data fields, thresholds, roles, schedule, IP, no-go criteria, possible PhD topic.
plan.terms: Negotiable: NDA covers board data; Nexara retains design data ownership; rule code and results ownership or licence to be agreed; publication only after Nexara review; costs, equipment recovery and any PhD arrangement decided separately.

issues: plan.metrics: go/no-go is ambiguous. Define a numeric false-positive limit and how the score threshold is fixed (e.g. set in advance, not tuned on the five boards). Define what counts as a scan hotspot coincidence.
plan.metrics: add a kickoff pre-check that the pre-compliance scans give hotspot localisation or band data mappable to layout features. Make failure of this check an explicit no-go.

plan.experiment: the HyperLynx emission-check step assumes the existing licences support it. Sources say only that they are mainly used for impedance checks. Add a kickoff item to verify this, and drop the step if it fails.
plan.dataRequired: the tool needs a netlist, but Nexara only offers Gerbers, BOM and scans. Add a fallback if netlists cannot be supplied, e.g. regenerate them from design files or narrow the scope.
